newsitem.title: USA: Xerox sees stronger dollar hurting 1997.
newsitem.headline: Xerox sees stronger dollar hurting 1997.

text.p: Xerox Corp said Tuesday a continued strong dollar will hurt its full-year 1997 results, but it is maintaining its focus on expense controls in its drive to deliver double-digit earnings growth.

In the first quarter Xerox said its revenue growth was hurt by a stronger dollar. Revenues were up five percent to $4 billion before the impact of currency. After the impact of currency, revenues grew two percent.
Xerox said a drop in paper prices reduced its overall revenue growth by more than one percentage point.
Equipment sales grew 10 percent in the quarter, it said.
Xerox said its biggest first quarter revenue growth came from its document outsourcing business, which grew 41 percent.
In the U.S., its revenues grew six percent.
Revenues from international operations were up three percent, before the impact from currency, reflecting continued difficult economic environments in several European countries.
Xerox also said it saw modest growth in the quarter in Brazil following an exceptional fourth quarter.
Operating margins improved by 0.8 percentage point due to an increase in gross margins and a reduction in the ratio of selling, administrative and general expenses to revenues.
Its digital products, which had revenue growth of 18 percent in the first quarter, will help drive revenue growth going forward, Xerox said.

It also said prospective buyers continue to show interest in the remaining insurance units of Talgen Holdings Inc. Xerox said it expects the previously announced sale of its Coregis unit to close soon, with the disposition of the remaining units to be completed by year-end.
Xerox said that as part of its ongoing stock repurchase plan announced in February 1996, it had repurchased 8.2 million shares for $406 million as of March 31.
